WITH matched_data AS (
  SELECT
    t.telescregistry,
    t.observstation,
    t.bandusagepct,
    obs.lunarstage
  FROM telescopes t
  INNER JOIN observatories obs ON t.observstation = obs.observstation
),
station_avgs AS (
  SELECT
    lunarstage,
    observstation,
    AVG(bandusagepct) AS station_avg
  FROM matched_data
  WHERE bandusagepct IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY lunarstage, observstation
),
phase_avgs AS (
  SELECT
    lunarstage,
    AVG(station_avg) AS avg_bandwidth_usage
  FROM station_avgs
  GROUP BY lunarstage
),
telescope_counts AS (
  SELECT
    lunarstage,
    COUNT(*) AS telescope_count
  FROM matched_data
  GROUP BY lunarstage
),
total AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_telescopes FROM matched_data
)
SELECT
  tc.lunarstage AS phase,
  pa.avg_bandwidth_usage,
  tc.telescope_count,
  CAST(tc.telescope_count AS REAL) / t.total_telescopes AS fraction_of_total
FROM telescope_counts tc
LEFT JOIN phase_avgs pa ON tc.lunarstage = pa.lunarstage
CROSS JOIN total t
ORDER BY CASE WHEN tc.lunarstage IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, tc.lunarstage

assumptions.assumption: The two-step averaging (first per observatory station, then across station averages) gives each station equal weight regardless of how many telescopes it contains. This is an unweighted average of station averages rather than a weighted overall average.
NULL values in telescopes.bandusagepct are excluded from average calculations per the phrase 'missing values ignored', but telescopes with NULL bandwidth are still counted in telescope totals.

alternatives.interpretation: Average all valid bandwidth values for all telescopes in each phase, without first computing per-station averages. This weights each telescope equally rather than each station equally.
